claims.explanation: Vincristine kills cells by disrupting microtubules, and sensitivity is largely determined by the efficiency of the apoptotic response to mitotic arrest. Loss of FBW7 or high MCL1 expression protects cells by preventing MCL1 degradation, while intact FBW7 and low MCL1 sensitize. Additionally, multidrug resistance transporters (ABCB1, ABCC1) reduce intracellular drug levels and confer resistance.

features.basis: Loss of FBW7 prevents MCL1 degradation, paradoxically sensitizing to antitubulin agents by allowing MCL1 to decline during mitotic arrest (PMID 21368834).
High MCL1 expression protects cells from antitubulin-induced apoptosis (PMID 21368834).
P-glycoprotein efflux pump reduces intracellular vincristine and confers resistance (PMID 7214365).
MRP1 overexpression confers moderate resistance to vincristine (PMID 7954421).
TP53 mutations are common in selectively killed lines, possibly due to impaired DNA damage response or mitotic checkpoint.
KRAS mutations appear in several sensitive lines, potentially linking oncogenic signaling to increased mitotic dependence.
PTEN loss is observed in multiple sensitive lines, possibly via PI3K/AKT-mediated survival signaling.
CDKN2A deletions/mutations are frequent in sensitive lines, suggesting cell cycle deregulation enhances sensitivity.
SMARCA4 mutations appear in several sensitive lines, possibly through chromatin remodeling effects on apoptosis.
BRAF mutations are present in some resistant melanoma lines, suggesting MAPK pathway activation may protect.
ARID1A mutations are enriched in resistant lines, possibly due to altered chromatin states.
SF3B1 mutations appear in resistant lines, potentially affecting splicing of apoptotic regulators.
